question: Will twitter / x.com be open source before September?
resolution_criteria:
[tweet]resolves YES if X publicly releases source covering the substantial core of the platform (backend serving, ranking, client apps), with narrow exclusions permitted for credentials, third-party proprietary dependencies, and genuinely security-sensitive modules — but NOT if the release is limited to the recommendation algorithm or another subsystem

Update 2026-07-27 (PST) (AI summary of creator comment): - The timezone used to determine when September begins is Central Daylight Time (CDT).

# Research report 1 of 2

Musk promised in July 2026 to open-source X's entire codebase "next month," but by August 25 I found nothing showing a release that would meet the bar. The only August release I could confirm is the For You ranking algorithm, which the criteria rule out. Every page fetch failed (the proxy refused the connection), so everything below comes from search-result summaries and I could not check it against the original articles.

## 1. Resolution source
- No URL is given. The question resolves on whether X publicly releases the core platform: backend serving, ranking and client apps. The likely places to see that are X/Musk posts and X's GitHub (the existing algorithm repo is xai-org/x-algorithm).
- 2026-08-25: I found no full-platform repository or release announcement. According to one tracker, the xai-org/x-algorithm repo had no push from May 2026 until the August algorithm update. [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/x-algorithm-open-source-github-elon-musk-2026)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The only August release I found covers the For You ranking engine (scoring weights and visibility filters), and the criteria explicitly exclude a release limited to the recommendation algorithm.
- Musk set "next month" (August) as the target. That leaves about 6 days before September begins in CDT, with no confirmed release.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-13/14: X widened the open-source For You feed code to include its core ranking engine, scoring weights and visibility filters, among them a filter for Brazil's 2026 election. TechCrunch dates it Aug 13 and an X post dated Aug 14 calls it "today's" release. Reports did not describe it as the full codebase. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/13/x-open-sources-its-ranking-algorithm-letting-users-see-if-theyve-been-shadowbanned/), [X trending](https://x.com/i/trending/2087960858571792703)
- 2026-08-03: The full release had not happened. It was blocked on an internal security review with no firm completion date. [byteiota](https://byteiota.com/x-is-open-sourcing-its-codebase-what-developers-need-to-know/)
- 2026-07-27: Media reported Musk's August target. [Dataconomy](https://dataconomy.com/2026/07/27/x-to-open-source-full-codebase-in-august-musk-says/), [TechBriefly](https://techbriefly.com/2026/07/27/elon-musk-plans-to-open-source-xs-full-codebase/)
- 2026-07-24: Musk posted: "Next month, every line of code touching the 𝕏 system will be open source and third-party audited." [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/x-open-source-entire-codebase-musk-july-2026)
- 2026-07-16: The pledge followed reports that xAI's coding assistant, Grok Build, exfiltrated developers' repositories. [TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/320727/20260716/x-vows-full-codebase-open-source-after-grok-build-exfiltrated-dev-repos.htm)
- 2026-07-15: Musk posted: "Once we have completed our review for security vulnerabilities, we will make the entire codebase of X open source, with no exceptions." He said third-party reviewers would check that production matches the published code. No license or named auditors were given. [The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io/x-open-source-codebase/), [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/x-open-source-codebase-musk/)

## 4. Base rates
- 2023-03: Twitter open-sourced parts of its recommendation algorithm, not the platform. [It's FOSS](https://itsfoss.com/news/x-might-be-going-open-source/)
- 2026-01-20: X open-sourced the For You algorithm. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/20/x-open-sources-its-algorithm-while-facing-a-transparency-fine-and-grok-controversies)
- Coverage also notes missed promises:
  - an earlier promise to update the algorithm every four weeks
  - a December 2025 pledge to release "literally all" of X's code
  - the Grok 3 open-sourcing window

  [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/x-open-source-entire-codebase-musk-july-2026), [studioglobal](https://www.studioglobal.ai/discover/answers/search-fact-check-with-cited-sources-for-6a661fee6b10ab849409a67a)
- In more than three years of pledges, X and Twitter have only ever open-sourced subsystems (ranking and recommendation), never the core platform. I found no case of a large social platform open-sourcing its full production stack.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Undated (late July or August 2026): Tech Insider reported that Manifold traders put "11% odds" on X going open source before September, after the "next month" pledge. Manifold uses play money. I could not open the article to check its date. [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/musk-x-open-source-before-september-manifold-odds-2026/)
- I found no Polymarket or Kalshi market on this.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-08-31 (CDT): Musk's self-imposed "next month" deadline runs out.
- Possible triggers:
  - X announces the security review is finished
  - a new GitHub organization or repository covering backend, APIs and clients appears
  - auditors are named
- Possible signs of delay: Musk reframes the timeline, or X publishes only more algorithm and ranking updates.
- Things to check close to resolution: Musk's X posts, the xai-org GitHub organization, and TechCrunch or The Verge coverage.

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

I could not find any report, as of 2026-08-25, that X has published the core of its platform (backend serving, client apps). The only code released in August was another update to the recommendation algorithm repo, and the criteria explicitly say that does not count. ## 1. Resolution source
- No URL was given. The question resolves on whether X publicly releases source for the core of the platform before September begins in Central Daylight Time (CDT).
- The place to check is X's GitHub organizations. The only active repo I found is xai-org/x-algorithm, which holds the "For You" ranking code. I found no repo with backend serving or client app code. [cryptobriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/x-open-sources-for-you-algorithm/)

## 2. Current status
- I found no evidence that anything close to the full codebase is out. The question is not settled, and all public releases so far are subsystems, which the criteria exclude.
- 2026-08-03: one report said the release "has not happened" because it is blocked on an internal security review with no firm completion date, and no license has been announced. ## 3. Recent news (newest first)

It covers model configuration, filters and core ranking, reportedly 10 to 15 times bigger than the earlier release. X also launched an in-app shadowban checker. This is still only the ranking subsystem. One aggregator phrased it as "every line of code running the X algorithm," which is ambiguous about scope. [Muskonomy](https://x.com/muskonomy/status/2081302742681923999)

[The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io/x-open-source-codebase/), [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/07/60492572/elon-musk-says-x-will-go-fully-open-source-with-no-exceptions-as-grok-faces-heat-over-privacy-breach-and-jailbreak-vulnerability), [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/x-open-source-codebase-musk/), [ProPakistani](https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/17/x-is-becoming-completely-open-source/)

## 4. Base rates
- 2023-03: Twitter published part of its recommendation algorithm. Coverage says the promised updates never followed. [It's FOSS](https://itsfoss.com/news/x-might-be-going-open-source/), [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/x-open-source-entire-codebase-musk-july-2026)

[AlternativeTo](https://alternativeto.net/news/2026/1/elon-musk-has-announced-he-will-open-source-x-s-new-algorithm-in-a-few-days), [Dataconomy](https://dataconomy.com/2026/07/27/x-to-open-source-full-codebase-in-august-musk-says/)

[byteiota](https://byteiota.com/x-is-open-sourcing-its-codebase-what-developers-need-to-know/), [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/x-open-source-entire-codebase-musk-july-2026)
- Pattern: Musk's open-source promises about the algorithm or subsystems have shipped, sometimes late. No major social platform has ever open-sourced its full production backend and client apps.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not find a Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this question or a close one, and no expert forecasts.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The month Musk promised ends on 2026-08-31 (CDT). A full release, or a statement that it has slipped, could come in the last week.
- Things to watch:
  - Musk or @XOpenSource posts announcing the security review is done
  - New repos appearing under X or xai-org on GitHub
  - The named third-party auditors being announced
  - Any announced license
- Scope risk: a late-August release could again cover only the algorithm or "the X system" in a narrow sense, which would not meet the criteria.

- No sign by August 25 of new repos, named auditors, or a completed security review.
- Manifold traders were reportedly at 11% earlier, before the algorithm-only release; that is play money and likely lower now.

**(e) Scenarios**

- No: August ends with only the ranking repo. Musk either says the security review is ongoing or treats the August 13-14 release as fulfilling the pledge.
- Yes: in the last days of August, X publishes a large set of repos covering backend services and the web, iOS and Android clients, and the question creator judges it to cover the substantial core.

**(f) From base rate to final**

I start at about 4%. The explicit August pledge pushes up slightly. The algorithm-only release on August 13-14, the unresolved security review, the absence of any precursor signals, and only 7 days left push down. Releasing client apps and backend serving code for a platform this size without visible preparation is very unlikely, and the strict scope means a partial release would still resolve No. I leave a small tail for a surprise dump or lenient resolution, which puts me at about 2.5%, rounded up to 3% because the outcome is not yet strictly decided.

Probability: 3%
